Author: broken_promises

Summary: After surviving the tsunami, Buck finds himself drowning in an entirely different way. It isn't just the trauma. Following his desperate lawsuit to get his job back, the 118 has completely shut him out, leaving him to freeze in the chill of total isolation. Now, he is entirely alone. The silence left behind is deafening. Eddie Diaz is running on empty. First, he had to watch Shannon die. Then, a literal tsunami tore through Los Angeles, leaving Christopher traumatized and trapped in a cycle of endless nightmares. Through all of it, Eddie thought he had one anchor: Buck. The one person he trusted implicitly. The one person Christopher needed. Instead, Buck filed a lawsuit, shattering that trust and walking away when they needed him most. Now, Eddie is drowning in a blinding, volatile anger—and he has absolutely nowhere to put it. OR: Buck and Eddie are both drowning, each in their own way. As one suffocates in total silence and the other burns with unresolved fury, the life support they used to provide each other is completely gone. I can get tested for... you know, the standard stuff. It's not the end of the world. Just take a deep breath." Lucas let out a sound that was half sob, half hysterical laugh. He backed up until his spine hit the bedroom wall, sliding down slightly as if his legs could no longer support his weight. He looked at Buck like he was looking at a dead man.
